questions.stem: During an infection, which cell type within the innate immune system not only performs phagocytosis but also assists in activating the complement system to enhance microbial clearance?
Which method enhances the growth of Haemophilus influenzae on blood agar by providing an additional essential factor?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Co-culturing with Staphylococcus aureus

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following discoveries is most famously associated with this scientist ?

options.label: B
options.text: Development of the first synthetic antimicrobial drug

options.label: D
options.text: Formulation of the germ theory of disease

questions.answerText: Development of the first synthetic antimicrobial drug
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Development of the first synthetic antimicrobial drug

questions.stem: Which of the following media is used to culture Mycoplasma pneumoniae?
Which of the following statements accurately describes the transmission characteristics of HSV-2?

options.label: A
options.text: It is transmitted exclusively through non-sexual skin-to-skin contact.

options.label: B
options.text: It can be transmitted even in the absence of visible lesions.

options.label: C
options.text: It primarily causes systemic symptoms without localized lesions.

questions.answerText: It can be transmitted even in the absence of visible lesions.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) It can be transmitted even in the absence of visible lesions.

options.label: B
options.text: Ingestion of egg contaminated in water

questions.answerText: Ingestion of egg contaminated in water

questions.stem: A patient with a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli shows resistance to penicillins, third generation cephalosporins and carbapenems. Which of the following mechanisms most likely explains this resistance?

questions.stemHtml: A 29-year-old pregnant woman in her first trimester presents with mild fever, myalgia, and lymphadenopathy. Amniotic fluid PCR is pending. The organism below was identified on a Giemsa-stained sample. Which of the following is considered the test for confirming this disease?

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with a urinary catheter develops a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Investigation shows the resistance genes are located on a bacteriophage. Which of the following best explains the spread of resistance in this scenario?

A 35-year-old man who recently returned from Southeast Asia presents with intensely itchy, rapidly migrating linear skin lesions on his buttocks and thighs. The lesions appear to advance several centimetres within hours. He is otherwise healthy. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of his condition?

A 55-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with fever, facial pain, and periorbital swelling. On examination, there is black necrotic tissue on the palate. A KOH mount from nasal swab shows broad, ribbon-like aseptate hyphae with right-angle branching. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.label: B
options.text: Immediate surgical debridement and amphotericin B

questions.answerText: Immediate surgical debridement and amphotericin B
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Immediate surgical debridement and amphotericin B

questions.stem: A 33-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 count: 48 cells/mm³) presents with headache and photophobia for 4 days. There is neck stiffness and fever. CSF shows elevated opening pressure, low glucose, and increased protein. India ink stain shows encapsulated yeast. Latex agglutination test is positive. Which of the following drugs is most appropriate as induction therapy?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Amphotericin B with flucytosine

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man is diagnosed with chronic Hepatitis C infection. Despite therapy, he develops resistance to antiviral agents. This variability in viral population within the same host is best explained by:

A microbiologist is culturing a respiratory specimen from a patient suspected to have an atypical pneumonia. After prolonged incubation on PPLO agar, fried-egg colonies are seen. Which of the following stains is best used to visualize these colonies?

A 4-year-old child presents with recurrent episodes of cough, inspiratory stridor, and low-grade fever every autumn for the past 2 years. This season’s episode is more severe. Serology shows elevated IgG against parainfluenza virus. Which mechanism best explains the recurrent symptoms?

options.label: A
options.text: Reinfection due to lack of durable mucosal immunity

options.label: D
options.text: Cross-reactivity with other respiratory viruses causing false-positive IgG

questions.answerText: Reinfection due to lack of durable mucosal immunity
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Reinfection due to lack of durable mucosal immunity

questions.stem: All of the following are involved in urethritis except:

At a family picnic, multiple people develop vomiting within 6 hours of eating egg salad sandwiches left in the sun. No fever or diarrhea is reported. Stool culture is negative. Identify the biochemical test for which this organism gives a positive result.

During the management of a COVID-positive patient with hematemesis in the emergency ward, the following items get contaminated:A blood-soaked disposable gown,The patient’s hospital linen,Plastic oxygen mask, andA broken glass ampoule of ondansetron.Which of the following is the correct color-coded segregation of these items according to BMW 2016 (Amended) rules?

options.label: A
options.text: Gown & linen → yellow bag; mask → red bag; ampoule → blue box

options.label: B
options.text: Gown → red bag; linen → yellow bag; mask → yellow bag; ampoule → black bag

options.label: C
options.text: Gown & mask → red bag; linen → blue box; ampoule → yellow bag

options.label: D
options.text: Gown → yellow bag; linen → red bag; mask → red bag; ampoule → black bag

questions.answerText: Gown & linen → yellow bag; mask → red bag; ampoule → blue box
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Gown & linen → yellow bag; mask → red bag; ampoule → blue box

questions.stem: A 32-year-old traveller is scheduled to fly from India to Brazil. He is advised to get the Yellow Fever vaccine. Which of the following statements regarding this vaccine is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a killed vaccine given in 2 doses, 6 months apart

options.label: B
options.text: It is a live attenuated vaccine, contraindicated in infants <6 months

options.label: C
options.text: It provides protection for 1 year and requires annual boosters

options.label: D
options.text: It is administered intradermally and requires post-exposure prophylaxis

questions.answerText: It is a live attenuated vaccine, contraindicated in infants <6 months
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) It is a live attenuated vaccine, contraindicated in infants <6 months

questions.stem: Which medium is both selective and differential for organisms that can grow in high bile and salt concentrations?

A 62-year-old man underwent mitral valve replacement surgery 3 weeks ago. He now presents with persistent fever, a new murmur, and elevated inflammatory markers. Blood cultures are pending. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for his current condition?
A culture plate shows concentric rings of growth due to active lateral movement of bacteria across the surface of a moist agar plate. Which of the following organisms most likely shows this pattern?

A 32-year-old man from a hilly region presents with high-grade fever, rash, and headache. On examination, he has an eschar at the site of a mite bite. His Weil-Felix test will be positive for which antigen?

A 25-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with profuse watery diarrhea and abdominal cramps. Stool examination under microscope reveals small oocysts having 4 sporozoites & acid-fast staining positive. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

questions.stemHtml: A 40-year-old hiker returns from a trip to New England with fever, chills, fatigue, and dark urine. He is immunocompetent but had a splenectomy 2 years ago. Peripheral smear is given to you. Which of the following is the most likely vector involved in the transmission of this infection?

Further culture and DST (Drug Sensitivity Testing) reveal resistance to Isoniazid, Rifampicin, Levofloxacin, and Linezolid. Which of the following best defines his TB status?

questions.stemHtml: Match the following media to its organism.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3

questions.stem: Pepsin digestion of an IgG molecule produces which of the following fragments?

options.label: A
options.text: One Fc fragment and two Fab fragments

options.label: B
options.text: One Fab fragment and two Fc fragments

options.label: C
options.text: One Fab2 fragment and one Fc fragment

options.label: D
options.text: Two Fab2 fragments and one Fc fragment

questions.answerText: One Fab2 fragment and one Fc fragment
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) One Fab2 fragment and one Fc fragment

questions.stem: A 9-month-old boy has recurrent bacterial infections, absent tonsils, and very low serum immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, and IgM). Flow cytometry shows near absence of circulating B cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A stool culture from a patient with dysentery grows non-motile, gram-negative bacilli that show late lactose fermentation on MacConkey agar. Which species of Shigella is most likely responsible?
A 5-year-old child presents with fever, neck stiffness, and altered sensorium. Lumbar puncture is performed. Which of the following CSF findings is most consistent with pyogenic meningitis?

options.label: A
options.text: Turbid fluid, high protein, low glucose, lymphocytic predominance

options.label: B
options.text: Turbid fluid, high protein, low glucose, neutrophilic predominance

options.label: C
options.text: Turbid fluid, normal protein, normal glucose, neutrophilic predominance

options.label: D
options.text: Xanthochromic fluid, low protein, normal glucose, eosinophilic predominance

questions.answerText: Turbid fluid, high protein, low glucose, neutrophilic predominance
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Turbid fluid, high protein, low glucose, neutrophilic predominance

On examination, the child appears ill with swollen neck with thick, greyish-white membrane covering the tonsils. Throat swab showed this picture. What is the other name of the organism.

A researcher is studying gene expression in different tissues and wants to measure the relative abundance of mRNA transcripts. She isolates nucleic acids, runs them on a gel, and uses a labeled RNA probe to identify specific sequences. Which of the following techniques is she most likely using?

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who recently returned from Southeast Asia presents with itchy, linear, rapidly advancing skin lesions on his lower back and thighs. The lesions progress several centimeters per hour. He also complains of intermittent abdominal discomfort. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

A 30-year-old woman presents with thin, homogenous, malodorous vaginal discharge. On speculum exam, the vaginal mucosa appears normal. To confirm the diagnosis, which of the following combination of findings or tests is most specific for diagnosing this disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Budding yeast cells on saline mount and normal pH

options.label: B
options.text: Motile trophozoites and strawberry cervix on examination

options.label: C
options.text: Clue cells on wet mount, pH > 4.5, and positive whiff test

options.label: D
options.text: Thick curdy discharge, pseudohyphae on KOH mount, pH < 4.5

questions.answerText: Clue cells on wet mount, pH > 4.5, and positive whiff test

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient is undergoing a bacterial culture test. The organism grown from the sample is bile esculin positive and can grow in 6.5% sodium chloride. Based on these characteristics, which of the following bacteria is most likely to be the causative agent?

A 29-year-old healthcare worker presents for evaluation after feeling fatigued for a few days. He had a needlestick injury about 2 months ago. Lab results show elevated liver enzymes. His Hepatitis B serology panel is as follows:HBsAg: PositiveAnti-HBc IgM: PositiveHBeAg: NegativeAnti-HBs: NegativeAnti-HBe: PositiveWhich of the following best explains his infection status?

options.label: B
options.text: Chronic hepatitis B infection with low infectivity

options.label: C
options.text: Immunity due to past resolved infection

options.label: D
options.text: Early window period of hepatitis B infection

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Acute hepatitis B infection

questions.stem: A 28-year-old nurse presents with redness and itching on the backs of her hands. The rash appeared 48 hours after she started using a new hand sanitizer at work. On examination, there are well-demarcated erythematous and scaly patches. There is no fever or systemic involvement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and mechanism?

A 45-year-old orthopedic surgeon is preparing for surgery involving implanting a metallic prosthesis. The autoclave in the hospital is malfunctioning, and the technician considers alternative sterilization methods. Which of the following is the most appropriate method for sterilizing the prosthesis in this scenario?

A 7-year-old unimmunized child presents with high fever, cough, conjunctivitis, and a maculopapular rash that started on the face and spread downward. On examination, bluish-white spots are seen on the buccal mucosa. Which of the following vaccines could have prevented this illness?

A 32-year-old veterinarian presents with intermittent fever, night sweats, malaise, and arthralgia for the past 3 weeks. On examination, he has hepatosplenomegaly and mild tenderness over the lower back. Blood cultures are sent. Which of the following is the most sensitive method for early diagnosis of his condition?

A 65-year-old diabetic male presents with fever chills and non-healing ulcer on his foot. Pus culture grows pseudomonas aeruginosa. The microbiology lab reports zone of inhibition for multiple antibiotics. Which of the following is the method used here?

questions.stemHtml: What is the infective form of the organism whose lifecycle is shown below:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Embryonated egg containing L3 larva

questions.stemHtml: A 26-year-old man presents with high-grade fever, chills, and vomiting for 2 days. He recently returned from Odisha. His stained blood smear is shown below. He develops altered sensorium and hypotension within 24 hours of admission. Which of the following is the most likely reason for the cerebral symptoms in this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Capillary blockage by parasitized RBCs adhering to endothelium

options.label: D
options.text: Cytokine storm due to overactive immune response

questions.answerText: Capillary blockage by parasitized RBCs adhering to endothelium
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Capillary blockage by parasitized RBCs adhering to endothelium

questions.stem: A 7-year-old unvaccinated child presents with sore throat, low-grade fever, and a thick grayish membrane over the tonsils. On examination, there is cervical lymphadenopathy and difficulty breathing. Which of the following cellular targets is inactivated by the responsible bacterial toxin?

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a low-grade fever, mild malaise, and a bright red rash on his cheeks that looks like he’s been slapped. A few days later, a lacy rash appears on his arms and trunk. Which of the following best describes the pathogenesis of the responsible virus?

options.label: D
options.text: Integrates into host genome like a retrovirus

questions.stem: A diabetic man presents with facial pain, black nasal discharge, and nasal mucosal necrosis. KOH mount shows broad, aseptate hyphae with right-angle branching. What would you expect on Sabouraud Dextrose Agar?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Cottony white colonies turning grey-black

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man develops nausea, vomiting, and abdominal cramps just 2 hours after eating reheated fried rice at a party. No one else who ate other dishes is affected. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

questions.stemHtml: A patient presents with a scaly, ring-shaped lesion on the scalp. A skin scraping is cultured, and the fungal isolate shows the structures seen in the image. Which of the following dermatophytes is most likely responsible?

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with jaw stiffness, muscle spasms, and difficulty swallowing after a rusty nail injury 10 days ago. He was not vaccinated. On examination, he has rigid posture and opisthotonus. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of the causative organism’s toxin?

options.label: A
options.text: Inhibits acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junction

options.label: D
options.text: Damages 60S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting protein synthesis

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Blocks release of inhibitory neurotransmitters

questions.stem: Which of the following steps in the Ziehl-Neelsen staining technique requires heating to allow penetration of the stain?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Application of carbol fuchsin

questions.stem: A 32-year-old adventure enthusiast presents with fever, severe headache, and a rash that started spares wrists and ankles and spread from central trunk to extremities. He mentions removing several Louse from his clothes after a recent camping trip in the woods. Which of the following organisms is the most likely culprit?

35-year-old hospitalized patient develops a greenish discharge from a burn wound. Culture reveals a gram-negative bacillus that is oxidase-positive and produces a fruity odour. All of the following conditions are associated with this organism except:

A 40-year-old man from the Mississippi River Valley presents with chronic cough, low-grade fever, and weight loss. Chest X-ray shows a lung infiltrate resembling tuberculosis. A skin lesion on his upper chest reveals ulcerated verrucous plaques. Biopsy shows broad-based budding yeast. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 35-year-old scuba diver presents to the clinic with a painful wound on his leg, which he sustained while brushing against coral during a dive. The area is red, swollen, and slightly warm to the touch. The physician suspects a bacterial infection commonly associated with coral cuts. Which organism is most likely responsible for this infection?

questions.stemHtml: A patient with fever, cough, and recent hotel stay has negative sputum cultures on standard media. The lab recommends a specialized medium for Legionella pneumophila. Which medium is used?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Buffered charcoal yeast extract (BCYE) agar

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with fever, malaise, and myalgias after consuming unpasteurized cheese. What mechanism does this organism use to move transcellularly and infect adjacent cells?

options.label: C
options.text: Secretion of collagenase to penetrate cell membranes

options.label: D
options.text: Producing toxins to lyse host cell junctions

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Polymerization of host actin filaments

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a low-grade fever and a painful, enlarged lymph node in his axilla. On questioning, he was scratched by a kitten about a week ago. Physical examination shows a tender, non-fluctuant lymph node without overlying skin changes. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

questions.stemHtml: Craigie's tube method, as visualized in the provided image showing different appearances in test tubes, is primarily used to differentiate which of the following bacterial characteristics?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Motile and nonmotile strains

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with a chronic indwelling catheter develops a persistent infection despite appropriate antibiotic therapy. Further analysis reveals the presence of a bacterial biofilm on the catheter surface. Which of the following is not a property of biofilms?

options.label: B
options.text: Increases antibiotic entry into the cell

questions.answerText: Increases antibiotic entry into the cell
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Increases antibiotic entry into the cell

Stool microscopy confirms helminthic infection. Given that many parasites penetrate the skin as their mode of entry, which of the following does not enter the human body via skin penetration?
